pending_findings.evidence: finish(): when job is None (create/assign failed) it only calls kill_pid_tree (taskkill /T, which misses a detached grandchild whose parent already exited) and returns contained=False without recording anything; when api.terminate/_wait_empty raises OSError it returns contained=False without appending the job to _OPEN_JOBS (handle also never closed, so KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE never fires). precheck() inspects only _OPEN_JOBS, so the next reviewer's containment_pre is contained=True. run_cmd ignores finish()'s result for gates. Repro with a fake kernel32: /tmp/uri_review_R2/probe_precheck.py prints 'implementer finish: {contained: False, job not created...}' then 'reviewer precheck : {contained: True, killed: 0}' and 'reviewer finish: {contained: True}'; /tmp/uri_review_R2/probe_terminate.py prints 'job 1 active: 1' then 'precheck: {contained: True}'. This contradicts the plan's design ('any containment API failure: contained=False (fail closed)'; 'Before each worker, every earlier job must still show 0') and the doc claim at URI_DEVELOPMENT_LIFECYCLE.md, and reopens the R8-01 threat (an earlier worker's process running alongside the reviewer) on Windows.
pending_findings.suggested_fix: Keep a module-level 'tainted' record: any spawn without a job, or any finish() whose terminate/verify raised, makes every later precheck() return contained=False (until the owner unblocks), or keep the failed job in _OPEN_JOBS so precheck re-checks it. Add fake-kernel32 tests for both sequences (uncontained implementer/gate then reviewer precheck; terminate failure then precheck).

report.notes: All 8 tests in test_lifecycle_dl2_repairs.py fail on f3706e0 (run in a clean archive of that commit with only this file copied in) and pass after the repair. Linux tests/dev_workflow: 220 passed, 5 PLATFORM-GATED (windows_only); it was 212 passed, 5 skipped before, and no existing test was removed or weakened. W-1: _test_file uses as_posix(). W-2: resolve_shim() turns an npm .cmd/.ps1 shim into the one existing .exe it names. reviewer_executable binds that exe (path, realpath, sha256) plus shim {path, sha256}, so a replaced claude.exe is drift/TAMPER. run_worker launches the exe directly and refuses (REFUSED, nothing spawned) a shim it cannot resolve; binary_is_default resolves the default the same way; the driver blocks REVIEWER_EXEC on an unresolvable shim. Ambiguity is computed on the resolved executables. Linux anchors are unchanged (no 'shim' key), so Linux runs in flight see no drift. A Windows run already bound to the shim will see TAMPER once and needs an owner unblock to re-bind. W-3 (test-only, tests/dev_workflow): fake CLIs are real .exe files on Windows (pip distlib t64 launcher + #!python + zipped __main__.py); gitconfig paths escaped (_gq); r1_06 uses a Python child instead of sh; r2_03 rewrites .git with r+ (cause of the Windows PermissionError assumed to be Git for Windows hiding .git, not confirmed); r1r2_01[False] uses an out-of-tree writer when fork() is missing; r1r2_01[True], r8_01 x2 and r10_01 x3 are marked linux_only, which conftest now reports by name as PLATFORM-GATED. Nothing on Windows was run here: the W-3 Windows outcome (17 failures expected to clear) and the W-2 Windows launch path are NOT VERIFIED until the owner-PC re-runs the gate on the new candidate SHA. Docs updated: URI_DEVELOPMENT_LIFECYCLE.md, LIFECYCLE_QUALIFICATION.md.

findings.evidence: On Windows shutil.which('claude') resolves to the npm shim %APPDATA%\\npm\\claude.cmd, a batch file that runs %~dp0\\node_modules\\@anthropic-ai\\claude-code\\bin\\claude.exe %*. reviewer_executable() hashes only the shim (interpreter=null), so a replaced claude.exe behind it is NOT detected as TAMPER (DEV-LIFECYCLE-1 R6-01 guarantee). Launching a .cmd also sends every argv item (including the --settings JSON deny rules, with quotes) through cmd.exe parsing, which subprocess list2cmdline does not quote for.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve an npm .cmd/.ps1 shim to its target executable, bind that executable's path and hash, and launch it directly (never via cmd.exe). If a shim cannot be resolved unambiguously, refuse. The parsing logic can be tested on Linux with a fixture shim file.
findings.title: Windows: the reviewer CLI binding hashes the npm claude.cmd shim, not the executable it runs; .cmd launch goes through cmd.exe parsing

findings.evidence: init(): when baseline.remote_branch is absent, base = rev-parse baseline.ref; 'expect' is optional. A config written in the old form ('ref': 'origin/integration/git-sync-20261008') reads whichever repository 'origin' is, possibly a stale tracking ref, with no canonical_url comparison. SKILL.md and TEMPLATE.json now use remote_branch, so this matters only for old or hand-written configs.
findings.suggested_fix: For a real milestone require baseline.remote_branch (or refuse a baseline.ref under refs/remotes/ / '<remote>/...') and require 'expect'.
findings.title: baseline.ref still accepts a remote-name tracking ref (e.g. origin/...) without the canonical_url check

findings.evidence: canonical_remote uses 'git remote get-url <name>' (fetch URL). integrate() runs 'git push <remote>', which uses remote.<name>.pushurl / url.*.pushInsteadOf if set. A remote with a canonical fetch URL and a different pushurl present at plan time would push the candidate to another repository. The subsequent ls-remote (fetch URL) then reports PUSH_FAILED, so there is no false INTEGRATED, but the outward push has already happened.
findings.suggested_fix: Also require that 'git remote get-url --push --all <name>' normalises to canonical_url, else BLOCKED REMOTE.
findings.title: canonical_remote compares only the fetch URL; push goes to pushurl/pushInsteadOf
